name: Inverse Rendering with Adjoint Derivatives
definition: An optimization method that estimates scene optical properties (position, scale, rotation, cross-section, spherical harmonic coefficients) from images using gradient-based optimization with adjoint derivatives of the forward pass.
summary: Inverse rendering with adjoint derivatives optimizes scene optical properties by computing gradients via reverse-mode automatic differentiation, uniquely propagating them through refractive interfaces and complex scattering events.
